# A Site and One Brand {#sec-sites}



The evaluation now has a report, a model card and a deck, in three formats each, scattered
across a folder. Investors, a client's risk team and a new colleague will each want the
latest version, from one address, and they will judge the work partly by whether it looks
like it came from one place. A small team has no designer for that. It has a site, built from
the same sources, and one file that says what the company's colours, type and logo are, which
every format then follows.

This chapter makes the evaluation a website with a home page, an About page and search, and
gives it one brand that reaches the site, the deck and the PDFs, and, through templates, Word
and PowerPoint. It ends with the checks a site needs and a person cannot make by eye on every
page: alt text, titles, descriptions, heading order and contrast, as code.

::: opener
- Say what one brand file reaches in Quarto, and how Word and PowerPoint get the same look.
- Ask for a website from an existing project: a render list, a navbar, a footer, a home page
  with a listing, an About page and social cards.
- Check every page of a site for alt text, titles, descriptions, heading order and contrast
  with a script.
- Decide where a branded site may be published, and what to set before it is.

Start from
: your `acme-eval` repository at the end of @sec-slides, or `checkpoints/16-eval-slides/`.

You build
: `_brand.yml` and a logo, Word and PowerPoint templates made from it, and a site of
  five pages, with a check script.

Checkpoint
: `checkpoints/17-eval-site/`
:::

## One brand, every format {#sec-sites-brand-reach}

A *brand file*, `_brand.yml`, states a company's look once: a palette of named colours, the
roles they play (background, foreground, primary), the fonts, and the logo. Quarto reads it
and applies it, but not to every format. Which formats it reaches decides how you build the
rest:

| Format | Does `_brand.yml` reach it? | How it gets the brand |
|---|---|---|
| Web pages and websites | yes | colours, fonts and the logo in the navbar |
| Reveal.js decks | yes | colours, fonts and the logo on each slide |
| Typst PDFs | yes | page and text colours, heading fonts, the logo |
| Dashboards | yes | colours and the logo |
| Word | no | a *reference document*, made from the brand by a script |
| PowerPoint | no | a reference document, made the same way |

: Where one brand file reaches, in Quarto 1.10.20 (tested 2026-11-18). {#tbl-sites-brand}

So the plan is one source of truth with two routes out of it: Quarto applies the brand where it
can, and a short script turns the same file into the two templates where it cannot. Change a
colour in `_brand.yml`, rerun the script, render, and every format follows.

## The brand file {#sec-sites-brand}

::: {.prompt .long}
```default
Add _brand.yml with Acme's colours from acme.scss as a palette and the roles primary, background and foreground, system fonts, and a logo at brand/logo.svg (a simple wordmark, marked in a comment as a fictional company's). Make slides.qmd use it (theme: [default, acme.scss, brand]), move every colour out of acme.scss, and make tests/test_deck_contrast.py read the colours from _brand.yml. Render the deck and the report, run the tests, and tell me where the brand's colours appear in each output.
```
:::

::: {.agent}
writes `_brand.yml` and `brand/logo.svg` · edits `acme.scss`, `slides.qmd` and the test · renders · `uv run pytest`
:::

The finished palette, and each text colour's contrast on the background,
\#fbfaf7:

| Used for | Role | Colour | Contrast |
|---|---|---|--:|
| body text | `foreground` | `#1b2733` | 14.5:1 |
| headings | `navy` | `#0b3d63` | 10.8:1 |
| links | `cobalt` | `#0b5cad` | 6.4:1 |
| captions, footer, slide numbers | `secondary` | `#4a5663` | 7.2:1 |

: The brand's text colours, resolved from the finished `_brand.yml`'s roles as its contrast test resolves them, with their WCAG 2.2 contrast on its background. {#tbl-sites-palette}


Verify where the brand landed, as the prompt asks: in the site's or deck's CSS, the colours
appear as variables; in a Typst PDF, they set the page and the headings. And make the contrast
test read the colours from `_brand.yml`, so the test checks the file that is now the source of
truth, not a copy of it.

::: pitfall
Three traps met while building and testing this step. The order of the deck's themes matters:
with `brand` anywhere but last, `acme.scss` cannot use the brand's colours, and Sass stops with
"Undefined variable"; the prompt puts `brand` last for that reason. A font list that ends in
the generic `sans-serif`, harmless in a web page, made Typst warn "unknown font family"; name
only real fonts in the brand. And figures drawn by matplotlib do not read the brand: the
finished project gives its charts the brand's ink and paper from a small helper that reads
`_brand.yml`.
:::

## Word and PowerPoint, in the same colours {#sec-sites-templates}

Word and PowerPoint take their look from a reference document (@sec-slides-pptx). Make both
from the brand with one script, so that a change of colour reaches them too:

::: {.prompt .long}
```default
Turn scripts/make_pptx_reference.py into scripts/make_reference_docs.py, which also makes templates/acme-reference.docx from Quarto's default reference.docx with the brand's colours and font (in its theme and its Title and Heading styles). Use it as the docx `reference-doc` of report.qmd and model-card.qmd, render both, and check the colours in the Word files.
```
:::

The check is in the Word file itself, which is a zip of XML: the theme's colours and the
styles' colours must be the brand's. In the test run, Quarto's default reference document
coloured its headings with the theme's first accent colour, darkened by a quarter, its links
with the same accent, and its title not at all, so the script wrote the brand's colours into
those styles explicitly. Checking the file, not the script, is what shows it.

::: pitfall
Two more from the test run. The project's `.gitignore` ignored every `*.docx`, as a rendered
output, so the new template could not be committed until it was excepted
(`!templates/*.docx`). And Apple's Quick Look preview showed the body in Times, ignoring the
theme's font; the finished script also names the font in Word's Normal style for viewers like
it. Check a Word file in Word, and in whatever your readers open it with.
:::

## A site from the project {#sec-sites-site}

A Quarto *website* is a project whose `_quarto.yml` lists its pages and how to navigate them.
Everything else on a modern site is vocabulary you can ask for:

| Ask for | Quarto calls it | Check |
|---|---|---|
| exactly these pages | an explicit `render:` list | README and notebooks do not become pages |
| a menu with the logo | `navbar:`, whose logo comes from the brand | the logo is visible against the navbar |
| a line on every page | `page-footer:` | the notice and the data's licence on every page |
| a home page that lists the documents | a *listing*, `type: table`, `default` or `grid` | each entry shows its description |
| an About page | `about:` with a template: `jolla`, `trestles`, `solana`, `marquee` or `broadside` | the logo and links render |
| search | on by default; `search.json` in `_site/` | a word from the report finds it |
| cards when a link is shared | `open-graph: true`, with `site-url` and a `description` on each page | each page has `og:` tags |
| the other formats of a page | Quarto's "Other formats" links (`format-links`) | the Word and PDF files are one click away |

: A website's vocabulary, and how to check each item (Quarto 1.10.20). {#tbl-sites-vocab}

::: {.prompt .long}
```default
Make this folder a Quarto website: _quarto.yml with an explicit render list (index.qmd, about.qmd, report.qmd, model-card.qmd, slides.qmd), execute-dir project, a navbar with the brand's logo, a page footer with the fictional-company notice and the data's CC BY 4.0 credit, site-url https://example.org/acme-eval/, open-graph, and a description on every page. index.qmd: a first sentence stating the headline result as inline code with a guard, then a table listing of the three documents. about.qmd: an about page with the trestles template. Render the site and list the pages and any warnings.
```
:::

::: {.agent}
writes `_quarto.yml`, `index.qmd` and `about.qmd` · adds descriptions · `uv run quarto render` → `_site/`
:::

::: {.you}
`uv run quarto preview` · open the address it prints, and the site on a phone-sized window
:::

The home page's first sentence is the headline, computed and guarded like any other: in the
finished site, v3 is named as the release that ranks best, with its numbers read
from `outputs/`. Its description, written once in the page's front matter, feeds the listing
on the home page, the search index, the page's `<meta>` tag and the card a chat app shows when
someone pastes the link. So write one sentence per page, without numbers, because a
description is front matter and cannot compute.

`site-url` is a placeholder until you know where the site will live; set it before publishing,
because social cards need absolute addresses for their images.

::: pitfall
Once the folder is a website, every render writes into `_site/`, a single file's too, so
scripts that expected `slides.html` beside the source must look in `_site/`; in the test run
the PDF and alt-text scripts failed until they did. And a navbar in the brand's primary colour
hid a logo in the same navy; `background: light` in the navbar fixed it. Look at the site, not
only its build log.
:::

## Checks for every page {#sec-sites-checks}

A person checks the page they are looking at. A script checks every page, every time. Ask for
the checks a site most often fails, as code:

::: {.prompt}
```default
Write scripts/check_site.py: after a render, check every page in _site/ for alt text on every image, a lang attribute, a title, a description meta tag and no skipped heading levels, and that the brand's text colours have a contrast of at least 4.5:1 on its background. Run it and fix what it finds.
```
:::

In the test run, the first run of the checker found two problems, both on the deck's page:
Reveal.js showed the brand's logo with no alt text, until the logo was given one in
`_brand.yml`, and wrote no description tag, until a short filter added it from the page's
`description`. Neither shows on the screen; both are exactly what the script is for. Each
check is a common failure with a reason. Alt text is what a screen reader announces in
place of an image (@sec-md-link-image). The page's language tells a screen reader how to
pronounce it. A title and a description are what a search result and a shared link show.
Headings that skip a level confuse anyone navigating by headings, as screen-reader users do.
And contrast is the rule of @sec-slides-theme, applied to the whole brand. The script does not
replace looking at the site, or a full audit such as Lighthouse's accessibility score;
it catches the regressions that a new page or a new colour would otherwise
slip in.

::: catchup
```default
Catch me up: follow ../quarto-workshop/checkpoints/17-eval-site/README.md
```
:::

## Where a branded site may go {#sec-sites-publish}

The site is static files in `_site/`, published like the London guide's (@sec-london-publish).
Two decisions come first. **Who may see it.** A public evaluation of a public dataset can go
on any public host; an evaluation of a client's data cannot. GitHub Pages serves private
repositories' sites only on paid plans, so private work needs a host your organisation
approves. **Where it lives**, so that `site-url` can be set and the social cards work.

::: tryit
Build the brand, the templates, the site and the check script, and preview the site.

::: done
one `_brand.yml` sets the colours of the site, the deck and the PDFs; the Word and PowerPoint
files are in the same colours; `check_site.py` reports no problems; and the home page's first
sentence names the best release.
:::
:::

## Summary {.unnumbered}

::: keyideas
- One `_brand.yml` sets colours, fonts and the logo for web pages, Reveal.js decks, Typst PDFs
  and dashboards; Word and PowerPoint get them through reference documents a script makes from
  the same file.
- A website is a project: an explicit render list, a navbar, a footer, a listing home page, an
  About page, search, and a description on every page that feeds listings, search and social
  cards.
- Descriptions are front matter and cannot compute: write them without numbers.
- Check every page with a script (alt text, language, title, description, heading order,
  contrast), and still look at the site.
- Decide who may see a site before choosing where it goes, and set `site-url` before
  publishing.
:::

The last of the evaluation's core outputs is the one that has to stand on its own outside the
company: a technical white paper, with references a reader can check.
